At later levels can also call in air-strikes on the path. |tooltip-2 = Units are capable of detecting [[Hidden (Attribute)|hidden]] enemies. }} {{QuoteContainer| {{QuoteBox|Send out a vehicle every couple of seconds to run over and shoot enemies.|Store Description}} {{QuoteBox|Send out a vehicle every couple of seconds to run over and shoot zombies.|Former Store Description}} }} __TOC__ ==Description== The '''Military Base''' is an intermediate [[Towers|tower]] that spawns various military-themed vehicles, which can be bought in the store for {{Coins|4,000}}. Levels 0-3 will spawn [[Humvee]]s of varying strength, Level 4 will spawn a [[Tank (Unit)|Tank]] and Level 5 will spawn a [[Railgun Tank]]. Periodically, the '''Military Base''' will spawn a [[Units|unit]] at the end of the path. The unit will head towards the start of the path until it gets destroyed, damaging enemies along the way. If it reaches the entrance, the unit will disappear. When there are enemies in a unit's range, it will slow down so that it has more time to attack enemies. For the first two upgrades, the main purpose of this tower is to spawn units with its ''Military Caravan'' that deal direct collision damage to enemies ([[Humvee]] and [[Humvee 2]]). After Level 3, the unit itself ([[Humvee 3]]) can deal damage through ranged weapons, and after Level 4, units spawned by the '''Military Base''' can deal ranged [[Splash Damage|splash damage]] ([[Tank (Unit)|Tank]] and [[Railgun Tank]]). The explosion is separated into two spheres. Enemies in the inner sphere will be dealt 100% of the stated damage, while the damage in the outer sphere is decreased linearly. Its splash damage deals full damage to enemies with [[defense]]. '''Military Base''' spawns can damage [[Lead (Attribute)|lead]] enemies through collision or splash, but not with their mounted guns. Both the tower and units are immune to debuffs, units being fully and while technically the tower can receive some debuffs, none of them can actually impact any of its stats. These units cannot be stunned, but they can be damaged by certain enemy abilities. At Level 4, the '''Military Base''' gains the ''Airstrike'' ability which drops six bombs in a cluster around on a specified path location

==Description==
The '''Damage Buff''' is a buff that increases a tower's damage, making them stronger. It is displayed on the tower itself with the icon of an arm with muscle.

==Mechanics==
'''Damage Buff''' range reduction is calculated as:
::<big>'''Damage × (1 + Damage Buff)'''</big>
:::where '''Damage Buff''' is the debuff supplied in decimal form (for example, 10% is 0.1).

The damage increased by the '''Damage Buff''' will always round down to the nearest integer. For example, a tower that deals 5 damage with a 50% '''Damage Buff''' will deal 7 damage, instead of 7.5.

Multiple towers are not fully affected by the buff. A full list of towers affected fully, partially or that are unaffected can be found below.
{{DamageBuff}}

==Applied By==
The following towers or consumables can apply the '''Damage Buff''' to other towers or itself:
*[[DJ Booth]] (Passive)
*[[Mercenary Base]] (Passive)
*[[Damage Flag]] (Passive)
*[[War Machine]] (Passive)
*[[Medic]] (''Ubercharge'' ability)
*[[Warden]] (When parrying)

The following event features can apply the '''Damage Buff''' to towers:

* [[Justice]] (Passive, [[Null & Void Event|Null & Void]])
* [[The Chariot]] (Passive, [[Null & Void Event|Null & Void]])

The following towers used to have the '''Damage Buff''':

*[[Militant|John]] (''Enraging Shout'' ability)
*[[Slasher|Shredder]] (''Knife Throw'' ability)
*[[Cowboy]] (''Wildest of the West and Gold Rush'' abilities'')''
*[[Gladiator]] (''Sharp Edge'' ability'')''

The following tower used to apply the '''Damage Buff''' to other towers:

The following removed towers had the '''Damage Buff''':

==Description==
The '''Range Buff''' is a buff that increases a tower's range. It is shown on the tower with a blue icon of multiple waves.

==Mechanics==
'''Range Buff''' range reduction is calculated as:
::<big>'''Range × (1 + Range Buff)'''</big>
:::where '''Range Buff''' is the buff supplied in decimal form (for example, 10% is 0.1).

The range of a tower affected by the '''Range Buff''' can be in decimal form, instead of being rounded down or rounded up to the nearest interger. For example, a tower with 5 range with a 50% '''Range Buff''' will have a range of 7.5.

The following towers are either partially or fully not affected by the '''Range Buff''':
*All [[units]].
*The [[Shotgunner]], as its bullets do not extend into the increased range.
*The [[DJ Booth]] cannot have its range boosted by another [[DJ Booth]].
**Other range buff sources, like the [[Ranger]], can still apply it.
*Circling range of the [[Pursuit]] and [[Ace Pilot]].
**The radius in which towers gain hidden detection from the [[Ace Pilot]] also cannot be increased.
**These towers' attack range can still be increased.
*The sentry building range of the [[Engineer]].
*The deadzone ranges of towers like the [[Biologist]] and [[Engineer]].
**The attack range for these towers can still be increased.
*Secondary orange range of towers like the range buff range for the [[Ranger]] or the gravestone range for the [[Necromancer]].
**The main range of these towers can still be increased.
*The chain range of the [[Electroshocker]].
**The attack range can still be increased.
*The explosion radius from [[Splash Damage|Splash Damage towers]] cannot be increased.

==Applied By==
The following towers or consumables can apply the '''Range Buff''' to other towers:
*[[DJ Booth]] (Passive)
*[[Ranger]] (Passive for 20 seconds at the beginning of each wave)
*[[Range Flag]] (Passive)
*[[UAV]] (Passive)
*[[Easter Egg]] (Passive for 20 seconds)
The following event features can apply the '''Range Buff''' to towers:

* [[The Moon]] (Passive, [[Null & Void Event|Null & Void]])

The following towers used to have the '''Range Buff''':
*{{Color|Golden}} [[Pyromancer]] (Passive)
*{{Color|Golden}} [[Cowboy]] (Passive)
*[[Slasher]] (Old ''Knife Throw'' ability)

The following removed towers had the '''Range Buff''':

title: Defense
wikitext_excerpt:
{{AttributeInfobox
|image1 = Defense.png
|type = Damage Reduction
}}

==Description==
'''Defense''' is a status value given to certain enemies and units. Enemies may spawn with this naturally, or be granted this through a litany of means.

==Mechanics==
There are two types of defense statistic. The main defense statistic is ''Percentage Defense'' which is used to calculate ''Effective Damage''.

''Percentage Defense'' is the actual defense percentage you see on an enemy or unit. However, this does not mean that if an enemy has 50% defense damage dealt towards it will be decreased 50%. In reality, the number listed is far closer to the percentage of additional health that '''Defense''' gives it.

''Effective Damage'' is the actual damage dealt towards an enemy by a tower once ''Percentage Defense'' is applied. ''Effective Damage'' is calculated by calculating

::<big>'''Original Damage ÷ (1 + Percentage Defense)'''</big>

where ''Percentage Defense'' is changed from a percentage into its equivalent decimal number (for instance, 50% would be 0.5 in decimal form). For example, a tower that deals 100 damage attacking an enemy with 50% defense would deal 67 damage as 100 ÷ (1 + 0.5) = 66.67 to two decimal places. Due to ''Effective Damage'' always being rounded up to the nearest integer, 66.67 rounds up to 67. Prior to the [[v1.1.0|Entity System Update]], ''Effective Damage'' was always rounded down to the nearest integer.

Unit defense works identically to enemy defense, reducing damage from enemy abilities and collision.

A list of certain ''Percentage Defense'' values and how much damage they actually reduce has been provided below. This is not a comprehensive list and the values may not be fully accurate due to how the game rounds up the damage, making the values occasionally lower.

===Countering Defense===
'''Defense''' can reduce the damage output of most towers significantly.

There are a couple of towers and consumables that can melt the ''Percentage Defense'' value of enemies, allowing your towers to deal more damage. A few certain towers can also ignore defense. There are two types of defense melting towers. The first has them decrease ''Total Defense'' by a certain percentage. However, if the [[Pyromancer]], which melts defense by 50%, is decreasing defense of [[Fallen Hero]], which has 50% defense, this does not mean its defense will be lowered to 0%. Instead, it is decreased by 25% defense, as which is 50% of 50% defense. The defense removal can stack, so the [[Pyromancer]] and [[Electroshocker]] can together remove 70% ''Percentage Defense'', but two [[Pyromancer]]s cannot remove 100% ''Percentage Defense''. Instead, only 50% ''Percentage Defense'' can be melted. Additionally, defense melting from burn cannot stack with other burn towers, freeze defense melting cannot stack with other freeze towers and poison defense melting cannot stack with other poison towers.

The second type has them decrease ''Total Defense'' by a flat amount. For example, the [[DJ Booth]] at maximum power can melt 25% defense. This means that when melting defense of the [[Fallen Giant]], it will will melt its defense from 60% to 35%.

Both forms of defense melting do not interfere with each other and can stack. For example, if the [[DJ Booth]] decreases the [[Vindicator (Legacy)|Vindicator]]'s defense from 100% to 75%, the [[Pyromancer]] will reduce it from 75% to 25%, which is the same decrease (50% less defense) as if [[DJ Booth]] did not affect it. Likewise, if the [[Pyromancer]] decreases the [[Vindicator (Legacy)|Vindicator]]'s defense from 100% to 50%, the [[DJ Booth]] will still be able to decrease it by 25%, from 50% to 25%.

Towers need flying detection to target these enemies. ==Mechanics== '''Flying''' enemies fly above the path, which grants them multiple perks. The main immunity that it grants is requiring flying detection to target them, making it difficult for towers without said detection to damage a '''Flying''' enemy. '''Flying''' enemies have various other unique immunities that are applied, outside of flying detection: # They are completely immune to being damaged by unit collision damage, even if they would normally collide with each other. #*This includes the [[Gift Bomber]], which cannot collide with '''Flying''' enemies, despite visually passing through '''Flying''' enemies. #*Some units, like the [[Rifleman]] or [[Missile APC]], can detect flying enemies, even if they cannot collide with them. #They are able to fly over road hazards, namely the [[Trapper]]'s traps and the [[Harvester]]'s thorns (and by extension the [[Farm]]'s). #*The [[Commando]]'s missiles, can still affect them. #*The [[Barricade]] can collide with '''Flying''' enemies, but they deal unit collision damage. Therefore, '''Flying''' enemies are also immune to this. #They are immune to being knocked back by towers. This does not mean they are immune to other effects from attacks that knock back enemies. #*For example, the [[DJ Booth]] can still slow down '''Flying''' enemies, even if the purple track cannot knock them back. '''Flying''' enemies may be indirectly damaged by towers, even if they do not have flying detection. For example, the [[Brawler]]'s ''Reposition'' ability deals damage to '''Flying''' enemies, though due to their knockback immunity it does not knock them back.
